entities.name: Leprosy
entities.description: A chronic infectious granulomatous disease caused by Mycobacterium leprae (and rarely Mycobacterium lepromatosis), predominantly affecting superficial cooler tissues including Schwann cells of the peripheral nervous system and cutaneous macrophages, leading to distinctive anesthetic skin lesions, peripheral nerve trunk enlargement, and progressive sensory and motor deformities.

entities.name: Prolonged Household Contact with Untreated Multibacillary Patient via Respiratory Droplets
entities.description: Prolonged, intimate household contact with an untreated multibacillary leprosy patient shedding infectious Mycobacterium leprae bacilli through respiratory droplets and nasal mucosal secretions during coughing and sneezing.

entities.name: Direct Contact with or Handling of Wild Nine-Banded Armadillos (Dasypus novemcinctus)
entities.description: Zoonotic exposure through handling, hunting, butchering, or consuming wild nine-banded armadillos (Dasypus novemcinctus), which serve as natural sylvatic reservoirs of Mycobacterium leprae in the Americas.

entities.name: Extended Residence in High-Burden Tropical Endemic Regions (India, Brazil, Indonesia)
entities.description: Long-term residence or exposure in high-burden tropical and subtropical developing countries, particularly South-East Asia (India accounting for >50% of global cases, Indonesia) and South America (Brazil), where sustained transmission occurs.

entities.name: Mycobacterium leprae
entities.description: An obligate intracellular, acid-fast, pleomorphic actinobacterium possessing an extraordinary tropism for peripheral nerve Schwann cells and histiocytes, displaying an extremely slow replication rate (12-14 days doubling time) and an optimal growth temperature of 27-30°C.

entities.name: Mycobacterium lepromatosis
entities.description: A genetically divergent acid-fast mycobacterial pathogen identified as a causative agent of severe diffuse lepromatous leprosy and necrotizing Lucio's phenomenon, primarily reported in Mexico, Central America, and parts of the Caribbean.

entities.name: Hypopigmented Anesthetic Skin Patch with Definite Loss of Thermal Sensation
entities.description: Well-demarcated or diffuse hypopigmented or erythematous cutaneous plaque or macule exhibiting objective, definite impairment or loss of thermal sensation (warm/cold), light touch, and pinprick pain, representing the cardinal clinical hallmark of tuberculoid and borderline leprosy.

entities.name: Enlarged Tender Peripheral Nerve Trunk with Associated Sensorimotor Deficit
entities.description: Palpably thickened, firm, and tender peripheral nerve trunks at superficial predilection sites (e.g., ulnar nerve at the medial epicondyle, common fibular nerve at the fibular neck, posterior tibial nerve behind the medial malleolus, or great auricular nerve in the neck) accompanied by sensory deficit or muscular weakness.

entities.name: Slit-Skin Smear Acid-Fast Bacilli with Intracellular Globi
entities.description: Microscopic visualization of acid-fast bacilli arranged in clumps or globi resembling packs of cigarettes using modified Ziehl-Neelsen (Fite-Faraco) staining on slit dermal smears obtained from cooler anatomical sites (earlobes, elbows, lesion borders) with a Bacteriological Index of 1+ to 6+.

entities.name: Facies Leontina with Madarosis and Infiltrated Pendulous Earlobes
entities.description: Characteristic leonine facies seen in advanced lepromatous leprosy caused by diffuse infiltrative nodular thickening of facial skin, deep furrowing over the forehead and cheeks, pendulous earlobe infiltration, and complete bilateral loss of eyebrows and eyelashes (madarosis).

entities.name: Ulnar Neuropathy Claw Hand Deformity with Hypothenar Amyotrophy
entities.description: Neuropathic deformity resulting from ulnar nerve trunk destruction at the olecranon groove, manifested by hyperextension of metacarpophalangeal joints and flexion of interphalangeal joints in the 4th and 5th digits, interosseous guttering, hypothenar wasting, and loss of medial hand sensation.

entities.name: Painless Chronic Plantar Neuropathic Ulcer (Mal Perforant)
entities.description: Indolent, deep, painless ulceration over weight-bearing points of the plantar foot (metatarsal heads or heel) caused by complete loss of protective nociception and autonomic denervation following posterior tibial nerve neuropathy, often leading to secondary osteomyelitis and trophic bone resorption.

entities.name: Lagophthalmos with Inability to Close Eyelids and Risk of Corneal Keratitis
entities.description: Inability to achieve complete voluntary closure of the palpebral fissure due to orbicularis oculi paralysis from zygomatic branch facial nerve involvement, exposing the cornea to drying, ulceration, keratitis, and secondary blindness.

entities.name: Type 1 Leprosy Reversal Reaction with Acute Painful Neuritis and Plaque Swelling
entities.description: Acute delayed-type (Type IV) hypersensitivity episode occurring in borderline leprosy patients, manifesting as sudden intense erythema, edema, and ulceration of pre-existing skin plaques combined with severe agonizing peripheral nerve pain (neuritis) and rapid loss of sensorimotor function.

entities.name: Type 2 Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) with Tender Subcutaneous Nodules and Systemic Vasculitis
entities.description: Severe immune complex-mediated (Type III) hypersensitivity vasculitis arising in lepromatous patients, characterized by crops of acutely tender, bright red subcutaneous nodules, remittent high fever, arthralgias, iridocyclitis, orchitis, and marked neutrophilic leukocytosis.

entities.name: High-Resolution Nerve Ultrasound Showing Asymmetrical Nerve Enlargement and Loss of Fascicular Pattern
entities.description: Bedside neuromuscular ultrasound demonstrating marked, asymmetrical cross-sectional area enlargement (>10-12 mm²) of peripheral nerve trunks (ulnar, common peroneal), architectural loss of fascicular echo-texture, and endoneurial hyperemia on color Doppler.

entities.name: Bedside Cutaneous Sensory Mapping Demonstrating Hierarchical Loss of Temperature and Light Touch
entities.description: Standardized physical sensory mapping of cutaneous patches demonstrating hierarchical sensory impairment where thermal discrimination (cold vs. warm) is lost first, followed by fine light touch testing with Semmes-Weinstein monofilaments, while pain/pinprick is lost last.

entities.name: Completely Intact Cutaneous Sensation to Temperature and Light Touch within Solitary Skin Lesions
entities.description: Normal, intact discrimination of cold, warm, and fine light touch across the entirety of an isolated hypopigmented or erythematous skin patch, which definitively rules out tuberculoid and borderline forms of leprosy.

entities.name: Intense Cutaneous Pruritus or Excoriated Lesions
entities.description: Presence of intense, severe itching, scratching, or linear excoriations within skin lesions, which is characteristic of eczema, scabies, or allergic dermatoses and effectively rules out leprosy lesions that are characteristically anesthetic and non-pruritic.

entities.name: Rapid Acute-Onset Symmetrical Distal Polyneuropathy without Cutaneous Patches or Palpable Nerve Trunk Thickening
entities.description: Acute or subacute, strictly symmetrical glove-and-stocking polyneuropathy lacking focal palpable peripheral nerve enlargement, mononeuritis multiplex features, or hypopigmented anesthetic skin macules, indicative of metabolic, toxic, or demyelinating polyneuropathies.

entities.name: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis
entities.description: A vector-borne protozoal infection presenting with solitary or multiple volcano-like ulcerations with raised indurated borders on exposed skin that possess completely preserved tactile sensation, spare peripheral nerve trunks, and show Leishmania amastigotes on Giemsa stain.

entities.name: Vitiligo
entities.description: An acquired autoimmune depigmenting dermatosis presenting with chalky white macules and patches characterized by complete epidermal melanocyte loss but entirely normal cutaneous thermal and tactile sensation, preserved sweating, and unaffected peripheral nerves.

entities.name: Pityriasis Versicolor
entities.description: A superficial fungal dermatomycosis caused by Malassezia yeasts causing fine branny-scaling hypopigmented macules with fully preserved sensation, normal peripheral nerves, and characteristic fungal hyphae/spores on potassium hydroxide (KOH) examination.

entities.name: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy
entities.description: A chronic metabolic length-dependent symmetric sensory polyneuropathy of feet and hands occurring in the setting of chronic hyperglycemia, which lacks focal cutaneous hypopigmented anesthetic plaques and lacks palpably thickened peripheral nerve trunks.

entities.name: Cutaneous Tuberculosis (Lupus Vulgaris)
entities.description: A chronic form of cutaneous tuberculosis producing brownish-red granulomatous plaques with apple-jelly nodules on diascopy that retain intact sensory perception and do not invade or enlarge peripheral nerve trunks.

entities.name: WHO Multidrug Therapy (MDT) Regimen Comprising Rifampicin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine
entities.description: Standardized World Health Organization multidrug regimen consisting of supervised monthly rifampicin combined with daily dapsone (for paucibacillary cases over 6 months) plus clofazimine (for multibacillary cases over 12 months), achieving bacillary clearance and cure while preventing resistance.

entities.name: High-Dose Systemic Corticosteroids (Prednisolone) for Reversal Neuritis
entities.description: Prompt administration of oral prednisolone (starting at 40 mg daily and tapered over 16-24 weeks) which suppresses acute cell-mediated intraneural edema, halts rapid nerve destruction, and averts irreversible motor deformities during Type 1 reactions.

entities.name: Thalidomide for Type 2 Reaction (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum)
entities.description: Potent anti-inflammatory immunomodulator providing rapid, dramatic clinical defervescence and resolution of painful subcutaneous inflammatory nodules within 48 to 72 hours in severe Type 2 ENL (strictly contraindicated in females of childbearing potential due to severe teratogenicity).

entities.name: Standard Beta-Lactam and Cephalosporin Antibiotics
entities.description: Standard broad-spectrum antibacterial regimens including penicillins, ampicillin, cephalosporins, and conventional macrolides, to which Mycobacterium leprae is intrinsically refractory and completely non-responsive.

relationships.target: Prolonged Household Contact with Untreated Multibacillary Patient via Respiratory Droplets
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Leprosy is predominantly transmitted from person to person via infectious upper airway droplets and nasal secretions during prolonged, close household contact with an untreated multibacillary patient.

relationships.target: Direct Contact with or Handling of Wild Nine-Banded Armadillos (Dasypus novemcinctus)
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Zoonotic infection can occur through direct contact with, hunting, skinning, or butchering wild nine-banded armadillos (Dasypus novemcinctus), which serve as natural sylvatic reservoirs of Mycobacterium leprae.

relationships.target: Extended Residence in High-Burden Tropical Endemic Regions (India, Brazil, Indonesia)
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leprosy acquisition is strongly linked to prolonged residence or travel in high-burden tropical and subtropical developing countries, predominantly South-East Asia (India and Indonesia) and Latin America (Brazil).

relationships.target: Mycobacterium leprae
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Leprosy is caused by Mycobacterium leprae, an obligate intracellular, acid-fast bacillus displaying unique tropism for peripheral nerve Schwann cells and dermal histiocytes.

relationships.target: Mycobacterium lepromatosis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Leprosy can be caused by Mycobacterium lepromatosis, a related acid-fast species responsible for severe diffuse lepromatous leprosy and necrotizing Lucio's phenomenon.

relationships.target: Hypopigmented Anesthetic Skin Patch with Definite Loss of Thermal Sensation
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] The presence of one or more hypopigmented or reddish cutaneous lesions demonstrating definite objective loss of thermal sensation and light touch is a cardinal pathognomonic WHO diagnostic sign of leprosy.

relationships.target: Enlarged Tender Peripheral Nerve Trunk with Associated Sensorimotor Deficit
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Palpably thickened, firm, and tender peripheral nerve trunks (such as the ulnar or common fibular nerve) accompanied by distal motor weakness or sensory impairment constitute a cardinal WHO diagnostic hallmark of leprosy.

relationships.target: Slit-Skin Smear Acid-Fast Bacilli with Intracellular Globi
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Slit-skin smear microscopy stained with Fite-Faraco modified acid-fast stain demonstrating clusters and globi of intracellular bacilli (Bacteriological Index 1+ to 6+) confirms multibacillary leprosy at admission.

relationships.target: Facies Leontina with Madarosis and Infiltrated Pendulous Earlobes
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Advanced lepromatous leprosy exhibits the pathognomonic lion-like facies (facies leontina) caused by diffuse nodular facial infiltration, thickened earlobes, and bilateral loss of eyebrows and eyelashes (madarosis).

relationships.target: Ulnar Neuropathy Claw Hand Deformity with Hypothenar Amyotrophy
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Peripheral ulnar nerve trunk damage produces a characteristic claw hand deformity (main en griffe) with flexion of the fourth and fifth digits, interosseous guttering, and hypothenar muscular wasting.

relationships.target: Painless Chronic Plantar Neuropathic Ulcer (Mal Perforant)
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Severe posterior tibial nerve denervation causes loss of plantar sensation leading to chronic painless plantar neuropathic ulcers (mal perforant) and digital trophic bone resorption.

relationships.target: Lagophthalmos with Inability to Close Eyelids and Risk of Corneal Keratitis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Infiltration of the zygomatic branch of the facial nerve induces orbicularis oculi paralysis resulting in paralytic lagophthalmos, corneal exposure, ulceration, and potential blindness.

relationships.target: Type 1 Leprosy Reversal Reaction with Acute Painful Neuritis and Plaque Swelling
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Type 1 reversal reactions present as an acute delayed-type hypersensitivity flare characterized by sudden erythema and edema of skin lesions accompanied by acute excruciating neuritis and rapid motor paralysis.

relationships.target: Type 2 Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) with Tender Subcutaneous Nodules and Systemic Vasculitis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Type 2 reaction (ENL) presents as sudden crops of painful, bright red subcutaneous nodules with high fever, arthralgias, orchitis, and systemic immune-complex vasculitis in multibacillary patients.

relationships.target: High-Resolution Nerve Ultrasound Showing Asymmetrical Nerve Enlargement and Loss of Fascicular Pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside neuromuscular high-resolution ultrasound shows focal or diffuse asymmetrical peripheral nerve trunk enlargement (>10-12 mm² cross-sectional area), disrupted fascicular architecture, and endoneurial hyperemia on color Doppler.

relationships.target: Bedside Cutaneous Sensory Mapping Demonstrating Hierarchical Loss of Temperature and Light Touch
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Objective bedside sensory evaluation demonstrates hierarchical cutaneous sensory loss where thermal sensation (cold vs. warm) is lost first, followed sequentially by light touch, while pain sensation is lost last.

relationships.target: Completely Intact Cutaneous Sensation to Temperature and Light Touch within Solitary Skin Lesions
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Finding entirely intact and normal cutaneous sensation to cold, warm, and fine touch within a solitary well-demarcated skin lesion firmly rules out tuberculoid and borderline forms of leprosy.

relationships.target: Intense Cutaneous Pruritus or Excoriated Lesions
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] The presence of severe itching, intense pruritus, or excoriated cutaneous plaques rules out leprosy lesions, which are characteristically non-pruritic, hypopigmented, and anesthetic.

relationships.target: Rapid Acute-Onset Symmetrical Distal Polyneuropathy without Cutaneous Patches or Palpable Nerve Trunk Thickening
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Acute-onset strictly symmetrical distal polyneuropathy in the absence of palpably enlarged peripheral nerve trunks or anesthetic cutaneous macules rules out standard leprous peripheral neuropathy.

relationships.target: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Cutaneous Leishmaniasis, which manifests with volcano-like ulcerations that maintain intact local sensation, lack peripheral nerve trunk enlargement, and show Leishmania amastigotes on smear.

relationships.target: Vitiligo
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Vitiligo, where depigmented chalk-white macules maintain completely normal thermal and tactile sensation, normal sweating, and no associated peripheral nerve enlargement.

relationships.target: Pityriasis Versicolor
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Pityriasis Versicolor, which presents with superficial scaling patches with completely preserved sensory perception, normal nerves, and fungal elements on KOH preparation.

relationships.target: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy, which is strictly symmetrical and length-dependent, lacks cutaneous anesthetic plaques, lacks palpably thickened nerve trunks, and correlates with chronic hyperglycemia.

relationships.target: Cutaneous Tuberculosis (Lupus Vulgaris)
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Cutaneous Tuberculosis (Lupus Vulgaris), which produces apple-jelly granulomatous plaques on diascopy with fully preserved cutaneous sensation and without peripheral nerve involvement.

relationships.target: WHO Multidrug Therapy (MDT) Regimen Comprising Rifampicin, Dapsone, and Clofazimine
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Leprosy responds curative to standard WHO Multidrug Therapy (monthly rifampicin combined with daily dapsone and clofazimine), eliminating viable bacilli and promoting lesion resolution.

relationships.target: High-Dose Systemic Corticosteroids (Prednisolone) for Reversal Neuritis
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Acute Type 1 reversal reactions and acute tender neuritis respond promptly to high-dose systemic prednisolone (starting at 40 mg daily), which relieves intraneural edema and prevents irreversible paralysis.

relationships.target: Thalidomide for Type 2 Reaction (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum)
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Severe Type 2 reactions (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum) exhibit rapid defervescence and resolution of painful subcutaneous inflammatory nodules within 48 to 72 hours of thalidomide therapy.

relationships.target: Standard Beta-Lactam and Cephalosporin Antibiotics
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Mycobacterium leprae is intrinsically unresponsive to standard empirical antibiotics such as beta-lactams, cephalosporins, and conventional macrolides.
